question: What is cash reserve ratio?

options.text: The portion that banks can invest in the market
The minimum balance to be maintained by a customer in the bank
The minimum amount of deposit that the commercial banks have to hold as reserves with the RBI.
The portion that banks must maintain before extending credit to customers

solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** is a regulatory requirement set by a country's central bank that mandates commercial banks
 
• It is the **minimum amount of deposit that the commercial banks have to hold as reserves with the RBI.**
 
• **CRR( Cash Reserve Ratio) helps** maintain liquidity in the banking system.
 
• By requiring banks to hold a portion of their deposits in reserve,
 
 
• the central bank ensures that banks have enough liquidity to meet the withdrawal demands of their customers.
 
 
 
• It is a t**ool used by central banks to control the money supply in the economy which is called Monetary Policy**
 
• By adjusting the CRR, the central bank can influence the amount of money available for banks to lend.
 
• A** change in the CRR can influence interest rates, lending capacity, and overall economic activity.**
 
• **For example**,
 
 
• During times of economic slowdown, a central bank might lower the CRR to encourage banks to lend more money to businesses and consumers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Cash Reserve Ratio can be calculated using the following formula:
 
 
• CRR=( Total Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) Cash Reserves ​ )×100
 
 
 
• Where:
 
 
• **Cash Reserves**: The amount of cash a bank must hold with the central bank.
 
• **Total Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)**:
 
 
• This includes the total demand deposits (savings and current accounts) and time deposits (fixed deposits) of the bank.
